disclaimer: Eligibility rules summarised from publicly available consular guidance. Final eligibility is determined by the destination country's consulate or government. This is research, not legal advice — confirm with a qualified immigration lawyer before filing.

paths.summary: Italy passes citizenship through bloodline with no generational limit on the paternal side and from 1 Jan 1948 onward on the maternal side. If any direct ancestor was Italian at the time their child was born, you likely qualify.

estCostUSD.note: Document procurement + apostilles + consular fees. Most cost is paperwork hunt, not government fees.

paths.outcome: Full Italian + EU citizenship + passport. Right to live and work anywhere in the EU/EEA.

eligibilityRules.label: Your Italian ancestor was still an Italian citizen when their child (your next-up ancestor) was born
eligibilityRules.explanation: If your great-grandfather naturalised as a US citizen BEFORE your grandfather was born, the line is broken.

eligibilityRules.label: If the line passes through a female ancestor, that woman's child must have been born on or after 1 January 1948
eligibilityRules.explanation: Pre-1948 maternal transmission was blocked by Italian law. There is a workaround called the '1948 case' (Rome court petition, ~€5–8K), but it adds 2–3 years.

eligibilityRules.label: No ancestor in the chain renounced Italian citizenship

documents: Italian ancestor's birth certificate (estratto dell'atto di nascita) from comune of birth
Italian ancestor's marriage certificate
Italian ancestor's US naturalisation record (or proof they never naturalised — NARA Form N-565)
Every birth + marriage + death certificate in the chain from Italian ancestor down to you
Apostille on every US-issued document
Certified Italian translation of every US document
Your own valid US passport
paths.lowIncomeNotes: No income or asset test at any stage. Costs are paperwork only. Many applicants use a 1948-case attorney on contingency. After approval, you can move to Italy and access SSN-equivalent (codice fiscale) + public healthcare immediately.

paths.fullName: Irish Citizenship via Foreign Births Register
paths.summary: If you have an Irish-born grandparent, you can register on the Foreign Births Register and receive Irish + EU citizenship. The rule stops at grandparent unless your parent registered before you were born.
paths.outcome: Full Irish + EU citizenship + passport. Right to live and work anywhere in the EU/EEA + UK.

eligibilityRules.label: At least one of your four grandparents was born in Ireland (any of the 32 counties)
OR: your parent was on the Foreign Births Register before you were born

documents: Irish grandparent's Irish birth certificate (long form)
Marriage certificate of grandparent (if applicable)
Parent's birth certificate
Parent's marriage certificate (if applicable)
Your own birth certificate
Your current valid passport (any nationality)
Two witnesses to certify the application form
paths.lowIncomeNotes: No income test. €278 fee is the only government cost. Application is by post — no travel required. Once registered, you can apply for an Irish passport for €80 and move to Ireland (or any EU country) without further immigration paperwork.

paths.summary: 2021 law restoring German citizenship to descendants of those who lost it due to Nazi-era persecution, gender-discriminatory pre-1975 rules, or post-marriage naturalisation. Broader than people realise — covers descendants of women who lost citizenship by marrying foreigners pre-1953.

estCostUSD.note: Mostly translation + apostille. Filing is free.

paths.outcome: Full German + EU citizenship + passport. Right to live and work anywhere in the EU/EEA. Does NOT require renouncing US citizenship.

eligibilityRules.label: You descend from someone who was: (a) persecuted on political, racial, or religious grounds between 1933–1945; OR (b) a German woman who lost citizenship by marrying a foreigner before 1953; OR (c) a child of a German mother + foreign father born before 1975

documents: German ancestor's birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde)
Proof of persecution / marriage record / loss-of-citizenship event
Marriage + birth certificates connecting ancestor to you
Your own birth certificate + passport
Certified German translations of all US documents
paths.lowIncomeNotes: Filing fee is €0 (zero) for StAG §5 cases. Only out-of-pocket is translation + apostille. German consulates in the US handle the entire process by mail. After approval, full access to German public healthcare + Kindergeld (€250/child/month) from day 1.

paths.summary: If you have a Polish ancestor who was a Polish citizen after 1920 and the line was never broken by voluntary loss, you can apply to have your existing Polish citizenship confirmed. No generational cap.

estCostUSD.note: Government fee + archival research (Polish archives often require paid lookups).

eligibilityRules.label: Your direct ancestor was a Polish citizen on or after 31 January 1920 (when the modern Polish citizenship law took effect)
No ancestor in the chain voluntarily renounced Polish citizenship or served in a foreign military / government before 1951 in a way that triggered automatic loss
eligibilityRules.explanation: WWII US military service caused automatic loss under pre-1951 Polish law. Service after 1951 is fine. There are exceptions.

documents: Polish ancestor's birth, marriage, and (if applicable) death certificates from Polish civil registry
Proof of Polish citizenship: pre-WWII Polish passport, military record, or census entry
Naturalisation records (or absence thereof) for each generation in the US
Your birth certificate + parents' + grandparents'
Sworn Polish translations of all foreign documents
paths.lowIncomeNotes: Filing fee is ~€60. Archival research is the main cost — Polish State Archives charge per document. Self-research via PRADZIAD database is free if you read Polish or use a translator app. No interview, no travel to Poland required.

paths.summary: If you have a Hungarian ancestor and you speak basic Hungarian, you can apply for citizenship under the simplified procedure. No residency requirement. Language is the practical gate.

estCostUSD.note: Government filing free; cost is translation, document procurement, and Hungarian-language tutoring.

eligibilityRules.label: At least one direct ancestor was a Hungarian citizen (under the pre-Trianon 1920 borders this includes parts of modern Romania, Slovakia, Serbia, Ukraine, Croatia)
You can demonstrate basic conversational Hungarian (A2-equivalent) at the consular interview
eligibilityRules.explanation: This is the real gate. Most US applicants need 6–18 months of study to pass. Free apps (Drops, Memrise) + Pimsleur cover the threshold.

documents: Hungarian ancestor's birth + marriage + death certificates
Connecting documents from ancestor to you
Your CV/résumé in Hungarian
Photo IDs of you and parents
Sworn Hungarian translations
paths.lowIncomeNotes: No filing fee. Main cost is the language requirement — budget 6–18 months of self-study. Once Hungarian, full EU citizenship including right to relocate to any of 27 EU member states under Schengen rules.
